title: The Imperative (Fiʿl al-Amr)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 17; Ryding Ch. 35)
objectives: Derive the positive 2nd-person imperative from the jussive stem.
Determine the vowel of prosthetic hamzat al-waṣl (ḍammah vs. kasrah) from the middle radical.
Pair positive imperatives with negative prohibitions (لَا + jussive).
recallPrompt: From Chapter 16: How do you form a negative command ('Do not write!')?

sections.heading: Deriving the Imperative from the Jussive
sections.body: Form the 2nd-person imperative (fiʿl al-amr) in two steps from the 2nd-person jussive: (1) remove the imperfect prefix تَـ; (2) if the resulting stem begins with a vowelless consonant (two consonants in a row), prefix a prosthetic hamzat al-waṣl (ا).

sections.label: Prosthetic Vowel Rule
sections.summary: In Form I imperatives, prosthetic hamzat al-waṣl takes ḍammah (اُ) if the middle radical vowel is ḍammah (e.g., تَكْتُبْ → اُكْتُبْ), and kasrah (اِ) if the middle radical vowel is fatḥah or kasrah (e.g., تَذْهَبْ → اِذْهَبْ، تَجْلِسْ → اِجْلِسْ).

sections.translation: Write the lesson and do not play.
sections.irab: اُكْتُبِ: فِعْلُ أَمْرٍ مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى السُّكُونِ | وَلَا تَلْعَبْ: لَا نَاهِيَةٌ، تَلْعَبْ مَجْزُومٌ بِالسُّكُونِ
sections.notes: Positive commands use fiʿl al-amr; negative commands always use لَا + jussive.

sections.heading: Connected Reading
sections.body: Because the initial alif of a Form I imperative is hamzat al-waṣl, it elides after a preceding vowel: وَاقْرَأْ is read wa-qraʾ.
